To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
peer teaching is feasible, that students can be trained to take on the role of teacher, and that the students themselves report positive outcomes from the experience.

(1) peer teaching is an established practice that can be used in the EFL classroom to encourage learner participation; and (2) peer teaching can be used in conjunction with learner-generated materials to promote learner independence.

(1) students can be encouraged to create their own teaching materials; (2) students can be trained to teach their own lessons; and (3) student-created lessons can be successfully implemented in a university setting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how learners can be encouraged and supported to take on new classroom roles and how they can make contributions to L1 and L2 lessons.
the following questions: • How feasible is the concept of student-generated materials and student-led classes for a university-level English course in Japan?
the feasibility of making Japanese university students responsible for the content of their own English lessons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of peer teaching in the classroom is a valuable and beneficial practice that can be applied to all levels of learning, in a variety of different ways.
student-generated teaching materials are an important and valuable tool in the language classroom.
students are capable of producing and teaching their own materials and that this can lead to a more effective learning environment for all involved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students can be trained to take on a teacher role and to produce their own materials, but that they need guidance and scaffolding in order to do so.
the more students are involved in the planning and implementation of the course, the better the learning outcomes will be.
students’ participation in the design and delivery of their own lessons is a valuable pedagogical tool.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learners are not passive recipients of knowledge, but active participants who can contribute to their own education.
learners can become effective teachers.
students can and do make valuable contributions to classroom life, even when they are not yet fully competent in the target language.
